t: Listen to a talk on a business podcast.
Crowdfunding has become a popular way for entrepreneurs to raise money for their projects.
It involves collecting small amounts of money from many people, usually through online platforms.
These platforms allow entrepreneurs to bypass traditional funding sources like banks and venture capitalists, giving them direct access to potential customers and investors.
What customers can get in exchange is first dibs on the first products of their kind when they're eventually produced.
For entrepreneurs, one major benefit is that crowdfunding lowers financial risk.
By getting funds through preorders or donations, entrepreneurs can test if people are truly interested in their idea before spending a lot of time and money.
And the crowdfunding can create buzz and build a community around a product, which helps with long-term success.
Entrepreneurs must put in time and effort to create strong campaigns and keep supporters engaged.
Competition is high, and not every project meets its funding goal.
Even after raising money, it can be difficult to actually make and deliver the promised product.
Entrepreneurs need to keep supporters updated and be honest if problems come up—like delays in manufacturing or shipping the product—so they don't lose trust.
For example, there was this high-tech cooler for which millions of dollars were raised.
But production delays happened and weren't properly communicated to the financial backers.
The project never recovered from its reputational loss and went bankrupt, and many people who paid for the cooler never received one.
